campaign.title: Licensing for the extension family: the area answered as a function of the configuration, proved on the extension pilot

Phases 1, 2 and 3 landed on main as six commits (4147c72 the contract, 7f0f2b6 the specifications, c04397f the marker key of a dotfile, 5813703 the licensing engine, d3525b7 the extension family's answer, 4086164 the test of P4), the floor pieces of this machine green at the boundary: format, typecheck, runtime emit and check, type receipts, trace, docs, public formats, vibe check, specmap. campaign.mandate: Переведи на новую систему лицензирования (если там есть что переводить). Напоминаю, лицензия на [продукт] - это жесткая EULA. Посмотреть про то какую организцию и как нужно упоминать можно вот здесь: [репозиторий пилота первой кампании] идея должна быть та же самая: [продукт] принадлежит [правообладателю]
campaign.mandate-note: The mandate names the first consumer of the extension family, its rights holder and the first pilot's repository; all three are elided (`common/PROP-004` `NO-CONSUMER-PRODUCT-IN-THE-TOOL`; the holder's name belongs to the consumer's repository and the machine's trusted store, never to the tool, as the licensing-area campaign recorded). This plan calls the product the extension pilot and the earlier one the editor pilot. The holder is the editor pilot's: the trusted store of this machine records it under its profile in two forms (the legal name with its transliteration, and the transliteration alone), and the headers of own files carry the second form after the copyright year. The extension pilot takes the same forms, under a profile and a licence identifier of its own, because the EULA text names the product. The mandate's "if there is anything to move" is answered by this plan's baseline: the extension family answers no licensing area today, so the move needs the family's answer first (DEF-1 of the licensing-area campaign, narrowed here to the extension family) and the pilot second - the same order the owner chose for the editor pilot.

baseline.fact: `LicensingArea` (`packages/type-api/src/licensing.ts`): `headerStyle`, `licenceFileDirectory`, `componentLicenceDirectory`, `subsystem`, `fields` (role `expression` | `file-name` | `url` on an overlay target), `upstreamLicenceFiles` (path, component), `renderings`, `guard(ownRoot)` returning `path`, `suite`, `test`, `preamble`. `OPTIONAL_AREAS` pairs `licensing` with the capability (`projectType.ts:161-169`); `licensingShapeProblems` checks the shape. No member says where the family's runner starts, and no member says what the family's distributable leaves out.

The engine (`licensingSurfaces.ts`): the licence file goes to `licenceFileDirectory/<product.licenseFile>` (`LICENSE.md` by default, `licensingProfile.ts:34`); every upstream licence file becomes `componentLicenceDirectory/LICENSE-<component>.txt` from the bytes at the pin; the tool's own text becomes `LICENSE-codkit.txt` whenever `delta/own/codkit/` exists in the patch set (`componentSurfaces`, `CODKIT_DELIVERED_DIR` = `delta/own/codkit`, `licensingProfile.ts:40`) - which is also where `standards load` places the notice copy of every patch set, library or not. The guard template resolves every path from `process.cwd()` as the tree root (`licensingGuardTemplate.ts:183`).

The extension family is a configured type: every area is a function of `typeConfig` (`index.ts` `projectTypeFor(config)`, ##VSX-CONFIGURED-TYPE); the config schema is strict (`configSchema.ts`, `.strict()`) with the keys `ownRoot`, `extensionRoot`, `monorepo`, `packageManager`, `tagPattern`, `scripts{build,lint,test{command,ownGlobArg},package}`, `entryModules`, `localeManifests`, `cleanupWhitelist`, `packageScratch`, `outputs`, `stamps`, `watch`, `preview`; the overlay targets are the extension manifest and the locale manifests, fully open (`layers.ts` `openTarget`); the subsystems are `extension, webview, i18n, assets, build, config, docs, test` (`conventions.ts`); the brand guard lives at `delta/own/test/brand.leftovers.test.ts` and finds the extension root under the runner's working directory or as that directory (`brandTemplates.ts:223-228`); the words of a generated test come from the declared test command - `describe`/`test` for bun, vitest and jest, `suite`/`test` for vscode-test, `describe`/`it` for mocha (`generators.ts:64-73`); own tests run by the declared command with the own glob appended (`build.ts:98-110`), and the extension pilot's command starts the runner in the extension root.

The packager the family's `package` script runs (vsce 4.0.0 at the pilot's pin, `out/package.js:772-803, 1442`): files are sorted by path; the first file matching `extension/licen[cs]e` with no extension, `.md` or `.txt` becomes the licence asset of the archive and `vsix.license`, unless the manifest's `license` reads `SEE LICENSE IN <file>`, in which case exactly that file is taken; a file named `LICENSE` is renamed `LICENSE.txt` inside the archive. The family's distributable is everything the extension's ignore file does not exclude: at the pilot's pin the ignore file excludes `src/**`, `**/*.ts` and the build inputs, and names no licence file, so the upstream's `LICENSE` of the extension root ships and sorts before any `LICENSE.md` beside it.

The extension pilot (measured 2026-11-01 in its repository and fork tree): type `vscode-extension`, the upstream pinned at a tag, the upstream's licence file at the extension root and at the tree root byte-identical (MIT), no NOTICE file, the sources of the upstream headed by nothing; the manifest's `license` at the pin `MIT`; the own layer two sources and four tests headed by the four-line form `gen brand` wrote under a placeholder holder and a placeholder identifier, plus the tool's notice copy; nine resource files (two documents, seven images and fonts) and one overlay of the manifest; a placeholder licence file of the repository naming a person as the owner; `verify` clean (17 interventions) on 8a1b2a3; one release descriptor recording the distribution evidence as incomplete; the pilot's own campaign plan keeps its phase 5 (the policy, the declaration, the evidence) open for the EULA text.

The editor pilot's declaration (`codkitReleaseLicensing: 2`) and the machine's trusted store (`codkitOrganizationPolicyStore: 2`): one policy with the holder in two forms, `ownLicense` a `LicenseRef-` identifier in the organization's namespace, `ownLicenseScopes` over `delta/own/**`, `delta/own-extensions/**`, `delta/own-roots/**`, the permissive allow-list and the copyleft deny-list, and the custom licence's canonical text with its digest. The declaration's `product` block: `licenseFile`, `title`, `holder`, `year`, `retiredNotices`.

Gates on 8a1b2a3 (this machine, 2026-11-01): `npm run format:check` and `vibe check --quiet` green; the full Vitest suite is red on this machine on the untouched baseline (environment: timeouts, POSIX fixtures, `vibe install --offline` in the standards e2e), so only focused suites count as evidence, as the licensing-area plan recorded.

decisions.decision: The extension family answers the area in this campaign; the application family and `generic` do not (DESIGN-003 D11; DEF-1 narrows to the application family). Rejected: both halves at once (no pilot for the application family exists, and a family's answer is proved by a pilot or it is prose).

`headerStyle: 'line'`: the sources of this family carry no header of their own, and the four-line form is what `gen brand` already writes into the own layer, so own code keeps the shape it has. Rejected: `block` (the ruled comment of the editor's sources; nothing in an extension's sources to sit flush with).

The licence file lives in the extension root (`licenceFileDirectory` = the configured `extensionRoot`, the root itself for a single-package repository), because the archive is packed from there and the packager finds the licence file there; component licences gather in `<extensionRoot>/licenses`, which the ignore file does not exclude and the archive therefore carries; no renderings - the family has no installer; the subsystem is `config` (the manifest and the files beside it). Rejected: the tree root (not packed by a monorepo's extension); a new subsystem `licence` (the conventions are additive, but one more word for three artifacts buys nothing).

One field: the manifest's `license` key with the role `expression`, the own SPDX identifier the profile declares - the same meaning the editor family gives the key, and the profile stays the single source of the expression. Rejected: `SEE LICENSE IN <file>` as the value (a file pointer where the contract asks for the expression; the packager's selection is settled by D5 instead).

The archive must carry the product's licence file as its licence asset and not the upstream's: the area gains an optional member, `distributableExclusions` - for this family, the upstream's licence file of the extension root, excluded from the archive through one line of the extension's ignore file. `gen licensing` writes that line as a marker-block patch of the ignore file (an upstream text file with a comment style), `verify` checks the block is present and the guard checks the archive's sources no longer carry the file; the upstream's text still ships under `licenses/` by D6, which is what its licence asks. Rejected: leaving both files beside each other (measured: the packager sorts `LICENSE` before `LICENSE.md` and takes the first, which is the editor pilot's defect wearing an archive); `SEE LICENSE IN` (D4, and the upstream's text would still ship at the archive root as a second licence); a hand-written intervention in every patch set of the family (the engine exists to write exactly this). RP-1 asks the owner to confirm the contract change.

The upstream licence file and its component name come from the configuration: `typeConfig.licensing` with `upstreamLicenceFile` (default `LICENSE`, relative to the extension root) and `upstreamComponent` (default `upstream`), so the answer is well-formed for every configuration and a product names the upstream's open build as the editor family does (`code-oss`) - a type answers from the configuration, never from the tree (##VSX-CONFIGURED-TYPE). Rejected: reading the manifest's `name` at the pin (the tree); a required key (an unconfigured patch set must still have a well-formed answer: the empty answer would hide the upstream's text altogether once D5 excludes it). RP-2 asks the owner about the default name.

The guard: `delta/own/test/licence.leftovers.test.ts` (beside the brand guard), the words `testWordsOf(config)` answers, no preamble unless Phase 0 S3 shows the family's lint needs one, and the runner's directory as a new optional member `runnerDirectory` of `LicenceGuard` (the tree path the family's runner starts in, the root by default) so that the one engine template resolves the tree root from the runner's working directory exactly as the family's brand guard does. Rejected: a second guard template owned by the type (the licensing-area campaign's D8: one template, rendered with the type's words).

The tool's own licence text ships as a component only when the type declares `runtime-library` and the delivered directory holds the library: the notice copy `standards load` places under `delta/own/codkit/` is not the library, and a product that compiles nothing of the tool must not state that it does. Rejected: the current rule (the directory's existence), which would make every patch set of this family ship `LICENSE-codkit.txt` for a notice the archive does not even carry.

Codkit-side work lands on `main` in atomic commits per phase with the floor pieces that run on this machine; the extension pilot's work lands in its own repository and is not a commit of this one; the tool's texts name no consumer, no upstream, no holder and no legal entity (as D9 of the licensing-area plan).

Owner's amendment at acceptance (2026-11-01, verbatim: «Почему у тебя постоянно txt для лицензий. Я хочу чтобы был MD. Например, LICENSE.md. Кроме того, правильная капитализация: LICENSE-CODKIT.md. Запиши это где-нибудь в спеках, эта ошибка часто повторяется.» and «У нас нет старых клиентов-плагинов, поэтому тебе не нужно поддерживать совместимость со старыми версиями. Просто замени сразу на правильное»). Every licence document the tool authors is Markdown with the extension `.md` and a name in upper case: the licence file `LICENSE.md`, a component licence `licenses/LICENSE-<COMPONENT>.md` with the component's name upper-cased (`LICENSE-CODKIT.md`, `LICENSE-CODE-OSS.md`), the tool's notice `LICENSE-CODKIT.md`; the component names of a type's answer stay lower-case identifiers and the file name is where the case changes. Carved out: a rendering an installer dictates (`LICENSE.rtf`), the upstream's own files (never renamed), and the `LICENSES/<SPDX-id>.txt` form the REUSE specification fixes for a package's registry. The rule is written as a normative anchor in PROP-019 and cited from PROP-010 and PROP-006; the engine switches the name outright, with no reading of the old `.txt` names (no consumer of the extension family exists with them, and the editor pilot takes the new names by `gen licensing --update` in its own repository). Rejected: keeping `.txt` for component licences (the owner's amendment); a compatibility path for the old names (the owner's amendment; nothing to be compatible with).

predictions.prediction: After Phase 1, `licensingShapeProblems` refuses a `distributableExclusions` entry outside the tree-path rules and a `runnerDirectory` that is not a tree path, by the same contract suite that holds the other members; the editor family's answer, which names neither, keeps passing unchanged.

After Phase 2, on the stub fixture extended with an ignore file and a runner directory: `gen licensing` writes the exclusion as a marker-block patch, a second run is `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS`, `--update` after a changed exclusion rewrites exactly that patch, and `verify` reports one `LICENSE-SURFACE` finding when the block is removed by hand and zero after `--update`.

After Phase 2, the guard rendered with a runner directory passes when run from that directory and from the tree root alike (the unit test runs the generated file both ways under node's runner); the guard rendered today fails from the subdirectory - recorded by the same test as the pre-campaign behaviour.

After Phase 2, a stub patch set with `delta/own/codkit/LICENSE-CODKIT.md` and no runtime library gets no `LICENSE-codkit.txt` from `gen licensing`; one with the library delivered keeps getting it (the editor fixture's expectation does not change).

After Phase 3, `codkit types` prints `licensing` for `vscode-extension`; `projectTypeProblems` holds the pairing; the configured answer of a monorepo extension names `<extensionRoot>/LICENSE.md`, `<extensionRoot>/licenses`, the manifest's `license` key and the exclusion of `<extensionRoot>/LICENSE`; the words are `describe`/`test` for a bun command and `suite`/`test` for vscode-test.

The extension pilot, passed through `gen licensing`, `license annotate --own --replace-retired` and `verify`: zero findings; the archive built by its own `package` script carries `LICENSE.md` as the licence asset (the packager's log names it), `licenses/LICENSE-<COMPONENT>.md` with the upstream's text, no `LICENSE.txt` at the archive root, and no retired phrase in any text file of the archive; the fork-tree grep for the placeholder holder prints zero outside the tool's notice.

route.phase: Spikes and probes, no commits. S1: `vsce ls` (or the family's `package` script in dry form) on the extension pilot's loaded tree with a `LICENSE.md` placed beside the upstream's `LICENSE`, recording which file the packager names as the licence asset - read from the packager's source at writing time, the run confirms. S2: the engine's guard rendered for the pilot's configuration and run from the extension root - expected to fail on paths (`licensingGuardTemplate.ts:183`), confirming D7. S3: the rendered guard under the pilot's lint, recording any directive the family needs in front of the suite. S4: `gen licensing --dry-run` on a stub extension fixture with a store in a temporary home, recording every assumption of the engine that an extension breaks (the licence file in a subdirectory, no renderings, the exclusion). S5: `componentSurfaces` on the pilot's patch set as it is - expected to ship the tool's text (D8). Exit: the five findings recorded in the log; a red spike rewrites the affected decision in place before Phase 1.

Contract and specifications. `packages/type-api/src/licensing.ts`: `distributableExclusions` (an ignore file of the tree and its entries) and `LicenceGuard.runnerDirectory`, with their shape rules and the contract suite; PROP-016 `TYPE-AREA-LICENSING` amended; PROP-019 `GEN-LICENSING`, `VERIFY-LICENSING` and `LICENCE-GUARD` amended for the exclusion and the runner directory; PROP-007 `CMD-GEN-LICENSING` amended; new `modules/vscode-extension/PROP-006-licensing.xml` (the family's answer as PROP-010 states the editor's), PROP-001 capability list, PROP-005 the configuration keys of D6; the stub type fixture answers the new members; specmap and docs regenerated. Exit: `vibe check --quiet`, specmap --check, trace:check, typecheck, docs:check green; the contract suite green; P1 recorded. Commits: `feat(type-api): let a licensing answer name what the distributable leaves out and where the runner starts`; `docs(spec): the extension family's licensing answer and the amended area`.

The engine. `licensingSurfaces`: the exclusion surfaces; `genLicensing`: the marker-block patch of the ignore file (through the engine's add-block path of `marker new`), `--update` over it; `verifyLicensing`: the block present and its lines equal; `licensingGuardTemplate`: the runner directory resolved to the tree root, the exclusion checked against the archive's sources; `componentSurfaces`: D8 and the names of D10 (`LICENSE-<COMPONENT>.md`, no reading of the old names); unit and e2e suites on the stub fixture; FAQ and the command reference regenerated. Exit: the focused suites green; P2, P3, P4 recorded; the floor pieces green. Commits: `fix(licensing): licence documents are Markdown, named in upper case`; `feat(licensing): exclude the upstream's licence file from a distributable packed by an ignore file`; `fix(licensing): the guard runs from the directory the family's runner starts in`; `fix(licensing): ship the tool's licence text only with its library`.

The extension family. `packages/type-vscode-extension/src/licensing.ts` as a function of the configuration (D2-D7), the `licensing` keys of the config schema (D6), the capability in the manifest and the registry receipts, the type's suite over a single-package and a monorepo configuration; `modules/vscode-extension/PROP-006` to impl/done. Exit: the type's suites green; `codkit types` prints the capability; P5 recorded. Commit: `feat(type-vscode-extension): answer the licensing area`.

The extension pilot, in its own repository: the EULA text drafted from the editor pilot's text (the holder's two forms unchanged, the product's name, the upstream named with its licence and its components, the identifier in the organization's namespace), the profile added to the machine's trusted store, `codkit.licensing.json` v2 with the retired placeholder phrases, `typeConfig.licensing` naming the upstream's component, `gen licensing`, `license annotate --own --replace-retired`, a registry annotation for the resource files, `verify` to zero, `load --fresh`, the build and the archive by the pilot's own scripts, the acceptance of P6, the pilot's campaign plan advanced to its phase 5 and the legal review of the text left open as that plan's RP-4. This plan records only that the family's answer passed the pilot.

The application family's answer; `package`/`publish` refusal on incomplete evidence; the NOTICE section of modified upstream files; REUSE annotations written by `license annotate --own` for directories of data files; the guard over the owned roots.

risks.risk: The packager's licence-asset rule differs at another pin or version. Signal: S1 re-run at every pin change of the pilot; the archive's licence asset named in the packager's log. Plan B: the exclusion of D5 holds the archive clean whichever file the packager would otherwise prefer; a packager that stops renaming or stops sorting changes nothing in D5.

The family's runner refuses the generated guard (timeouts, module format, the lint). Signal: S2 and S3. Plan B: the preamble of D7 carries the directives; a runner that cannot run the guard is reported in the log and the guard runs under node's runner from the tree root, as P3 proves it can.

The marker-block patch of the ignore file conflicts at the next upgrade of the pilot. Signal: `reresolve` on the patch. Plan B: the block is one line with its marker and reresolves like any patch; the exclusion is also checked by `verify`, so a lost block is a finding, never a silent regression.

The full Vitest suite stays red on this machine. Signal: the baseline. Plan B: the focused suites named in the acceptance are the evidence, as in the licensing-area campaign; the full suite runs on the owner's Linux host when the owner asks.

review-points.point: D5 adds `distributableExclusions` to the contract so that `gen licensing` writes the ignore-file line of the extension family, or the line stays a per-product intervention the family's specification prescribes and the guard checks. Recommendation: the contract member - the archive packed by an ignore file is a property of the family, not of one product, and the editor pilot's defect was exactly a surface nobody wrote. Ruling (owner, 2026-11-01): «Да, план хороший, попробуй все это сделать.» - the recommendation stands.

The default component name of D6 - `upstream` (`licenses/LICENSE-UPSTREAM.md`) when the configuration names none, or the configuration key required once `codkit.licensing.json` exists. Recommendation: the default, with the pilot naming the upstream's open build in its own configuration. Ruling (owner, 2026-11-01): the same words - the recommendation stands.

The extension pilot's EULA is drafted in Phase 4 from the editor pilot's text with the holder's wording unchanged; the title of the declaration, the identifier in the organization's namespace and the retired placeholder phrases are proposed in the pilot's repository, not here. Recommendation: one profile per product in the store (the text names the product), the holder's two forms copied verbatim from the editor pilot's profile. Ruling (owner, 2026-11-01): the same words - the recommendation stands; the legal review of the text stays open in the pilot's plan.

log.entry: Plan proposed. Read at writing time, no commits: the packager's licence-asset rule (D5), the engine's guard root (D7), the engine's component rule (D8), the family's configured answers, the extension pilot's state after its move onto 8a1b2a3 (both notice copies refreshed, `load --fresh`, `verify` clean). Phase 0 runs the spikes that confirm the three readings before Phase 1.

Accepted by the owner with the amendment recorded as D10 (Markdown licence documents in upper case, no compatibility with the old names); RP-1..RP-3 resolved by the acceptance. The owner also asked what `--replace-retired` is: it replaces the retired placeholder headers of the pilot's own files, a one-time migration of six files, and has nothing to do with old versions of any client.

Phase 0, no commits. S1 run against the packager's own module at the pilot's pin: with `license` an identifier and both files present the licence asset is `extension/LICENSE.txt` (the upstream's file, renamed), with `LICENSE.md` alone or with `SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.md` it is `LICENSE.md` - D5 confirmed. S2 and S5 confirmed by reading (`licensingGuardTemplate.ts:183`, `componentSurfaces`); S3 moved to Phase 4, where the guard is first rendered for a real family. S4 found the assumption the plan had not: no marker form exists for a dotfile, because `extname` reads `.vscodeignore` as nameless, so the exclusion patch of D5 could not have been written at all - discovered work, entered into Phase 2 as the marker key of a dotfile (PROP-004 `MR-FORM-KEY`, the three ignore files in the shipped conventions, and the one dot-leading artifact name the file writer admits, `PATCH-NAME-ENCODING`); the pilot's ignore file at the pin is LF-only with a final newline.
